fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (75%) and deposit-normalized FCF yield (25%). P/E: NTM EPS at Sept 2027 of 0.25 x FY27 $9.16 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$11.19 = $10.68, less a 2% execution/permitting haircut to $10.47, x 25x = $262. FCF: NTM FCF at 80% conversion of NTM adjusted net income, ~$8.55/share, at a 3.5% yield = $244, plus ~$1/share of net cash = $245. Blended ~$258, about 6% above the $244.04 close.

inputs_detail.value: $9.16 (29 analysts, range $8.28-$10.94; $8.80 90 days ago, $9.10 30 days ago)

inputs_detail.derivation: I now use the aggregator FY28 consensus (~$11.19, range $9.55-14.39) instead of my round-1 $11.45. My +25% step-up relied partly on 'Q2 2026 orders +152%', which was really a Q4 2025 figure. +22% FY28 growth fits Dell'Oro's ~22% DCPI CAGR for 2025-2030, with net capacity additions peaking in growth terms in 2026 and moderating afterwards.

Cut from 4% because consensus is still being revised up and no peer has flagged demand cuts. It stays above zero for two reasons. First, delivery constraints are industry-wide: Modine had 450-550bp of margin drag, and Dell'Oro says 'the risk has shifted from demand to delivery'. Second, Texas has escalated from a grid-interconnection audit (2026-08-03) to a freeze on all TCEQ environmental permits (2026-09-21) with no end date. That can push some 2027 US deliveries to the right. Enverus's August view of 'big bark, no bite' predates the September expansion to air permits, which also hits behind-the-meter generation.

VRT is ~26.6x FY27 consensus ($244.04/$9.16), in line with Eaton at ~26.8x FY27 ($431.41/$16.12) and nVent at ~24.8x FY27 ($160.50/$6.46; I wrongly had nVent at ~32x on 2026 EPS in round 1). 25x is about the peer midpoint. VRT grows faster, which argues for more, but order visibility is lower and liquid-cooling competition is consolidating (Ecolab/CoolIT, Eaton/Boyd, Schneider/Motivair), which argues for less.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adjusted net income ~$4.2B ($10.68 x ~393M) x 80% conversion = ~$3.36B = ~$8.55/share; 3.5% FCF yield = $244; plus ~$1/share net cash at horizon

inputs_detail.value: $2.4-$2.6B guidance; H1 $1.58B, of which deferred revenue build +$1.82B and inventory -$1.05B

inputs_detail.input: FCF conversion of adjusted net income (NTM at horizon)
inputs_detail.derivation: In round 1 I assumed ~100% conversion off the $2.5B guide, but the 10-Q shows H1 2026 FCF was more than fully explained by customer deposits. Industry practice supports deposits persisting while growth continues: Modine took a $165M upfront payment on a $4B 2027-29 capacity deal, so capacity-reservation prepayments are now normal in this value chain. With ~20% growth in 2027-28, I assume deposits stop adding cash but do not fully reverse, and working-capital growth and capex absorb ~20% of earnings.
Implied by peer P/Es of 25-27x (Eaton 26.8x, nVent 24.8x FY27) at ~90-95% conversion, i.e. a ~3.4-3.8% FCF yield.

+$0.17B at 6/30/26, plus the implied H2 2026 FCF of $0.8-1.0B, less the $1.45B UIG payment at a Q4 2026 close, part of the up-to-$1.15B earnout and dividends, plus ~9 months of 2027 FCF. This follows the supervisor's reconciliation of the 10-Q and the UIG 8-K.

bear.story: AI capex digestion plus delivery friction. Hyperscalers guide 2027/28 capex flat after investor pushback. Texas's open-ended freeze (grid audit from 2026-08-03, TCEQ environmental permits from 2026-09-21) spreads to other states or delays 2027 US deployments. Customer deposits reverse as growth slows, taking FCF sharply below earnings. Share losses in liquid cooling to well-funded consolidators (Ecolab/CoolIT, Eaton/Boyd, Schneider/Motivair) pressure pricing. NTM EPS is cut to ~$8.50 and the multiple compresses to ~16x. VRT fell ~65% peak to trough in 2022.

base.story: Q3 lands at the top of the $1.77-1.83 EPS guide and the Q2 'timing' slip recovers. FY27 EPS comes in near the $9.16 consensus and FY28 near ~$11.2. The DCPI market grows ~20% (Dell'Oro), and data center capex (+92% in 2Q26) keeps the chain supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained. Texas is resolved through audits by early 2027 with limited net effect, since serious projects qualify and behind-the-meter power (UIG) gains. The multiple holds ~25x NTM, in line with Eaton and nVent.

bull.story: Rubin/Kyber ramps (Nvidia guiding ~70% FY28 growth) and 2027 capex near third-party forecasts of ~$1T lift demand and pricing. Industry long-term capacity agreements (like Modine's $4B deal for 2027-29) show buyers locking in supply, and Vertiv signs similar deals or resumes disclosing strong orders. EPS beats (FY28 ~$12.5-13) and the stock re-rates to ~29-30x, back toward the ~$380 52-week high. The probability is cut from 28% because I no longer have any current order data to support it.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$150 VRT would be ~16x FY27 consensus and ~14x NTM EPS at the horizon, far below Eaton (26.8x) and nVent (24.8x FY27), and close to the 52-week low zone (~$134-141). With peers still expanding liquid-cooling capacity (nVent's third expansion, Modine's $4B 2027-29 LTA) and Dell'Oro calling demand 'no longer the open question', a close there would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than 66%-vol noise. That could be: a second revenue miss blamed on 'timing' with deferred revenue ($3.63B at 6/30/26) falling without a revenue step-up; FY27 guidance below ~$8.5; hyperscaler 2027 capex cuts; permitting freezes like Texas's spreading to other major markets; or visible CDU/thermal share loss to the new consolidators.

key_uncertainties: Order visibility: Vertiv has not disclosed orders or backlog since Q4 2025 ($15.0B, ~2.9x book-to-bill). Deferred revenue ($3.63B) is the only hard proxy.
Cash quality: H1 2026 FCF was more than explained by customer deposits. Whether they plateau or reverse drives 2027-28 FCF.
Permitting: Texas's open-ended freeze now covers environmental permits, including air permits for behind-the-meter generation. Other states could copy it.
Durability of hyperscaler and neocloud capex into 2028. Third-party forecasts are ~$1T for 2027, but management teams have not guided.
Liquid-cooling share and pricing as consolidators scale: Ecolab/CoolIT ($4.75B, closed 2026-07-02), Eaton/Boyd ($9.5B), Schneider/Motivair, nVent capacity, and Modine's $4B LTA.
Multiple: VRT trades at parity with Eaton and nVent. AI-infrastructure sentiment can swing the multiple ±30%.
reasoning: Round 2 changes three facts. (1) The 'Q2 2026 orders +152%, $15B backlog' I relied on was really Q4 2025 data. Vertiv has disclosed no orders since, so I dropped my above-consensus FY28 (+25%) for the ~$11.19 aggregator consensus (+22%) and cut the bull weight from 28% to 24%. (2) The nVent multiple is ~24.8x FY27, not ~32x. The peer set (Eaton 26.8x, nVent 24.8x) is tighter and brackets VRT's 26.6x, so 25x is a peer-midpoint multiple. (3) FCF was deposit-driven: H1 FCF of $1.58B vs a +$1.82B deferred-revenue build. I cut FCF conversion to 80% and use a 3.5% peer-implied yield, which lowers that leg from $267 to $245. I agree with this point. From my own lane, capacity-reservation prepayments look structural in this chain (Modine received $165M upfront on a $4B 2027-29 LTA), so I don't model a full reversal. I also missed the Texas escalation, which is squarely in my lane. The 2026-08-03 grid-interconnection audit (ERCOT has ~474 GW of requests, ~90% data centers) was widened on 2026-09-21 to all TCEQ environmental permits, with no end date. Enverus's 'big bark, no bite' view dates from August, before the widening to air permits that also catch behind-the-meter generation. I treat it as a delivery-timing risk for 2027, not a demand collapse: Dell'Oro reports data center capex +92% in 2Q26 and says the risk has 'shifted from demand to delivery'. So I kept a small 2% EPS haircut and a slightly heavier left-middle. Consensus FY27 was re-checked at $9.16 and still rising (1 up and 0 down revisions in 7 days). Fair value: P/E $262 (75%) and FCF $245 (25%) blend to $258 (+6%). Scenarios: bear $135 at 24%, base $262 at 52%, bull $370 at 24%, for a mean of ~$257. The ladder is a mixture: 90% lognormal (median ~$262, sigma ~0.49, below the 66% realized vol, which was inflated by the post-Q2 drawdown) and 10% bust component (median ~$135) for AI-capex digestion or permitting contagion. That gives P(>=244) ~0.51, down from 0.535. I did not copy the supervisor's ladder. Mine is slightly more bearish at the center because FCF normalization and Texas both hit my numbers directly, and slightly thinner above $400 because I lost the order evidence that supported my bull case. No option data or priors were used.
